177855.overview:
Based on the arcade game, in Escape from the Planet of the Robot Monsters you are sent in on a rescue mission to Planet X. This planet has been taken over by robots and you must find and evacuate the remaining humans.

It's a shooter similar to Gauntlet, only with an isometric viewpoint. You run around the levels shooting robots, rescuing humans and picking up items.

One of the few major commercial title conversions from the Spectrum. While the intro screens were not changed, the game itself was updated to use the SAM sound chip and MODE 4 graphics.

459172.overview:
A game they said couldn’t be done; this sort of thing really should have been impossible…

Basically it’s like Smash TV on the SAM Coupé!

Shoot lots and lots (and lots) of enemies, collect power-ups and crisp packets, and advance screen-by-screen until you’ve beaten the big bad B.U.T.T. (Bugs Unified Terrorist Team). Players must collect five crisp packets to advance to the next level.

The game was released on two floppy disks, the first disk containing an animated intro, and the second disk the game itself.

459600.overview:
Infamous "conversion" of the ZX Spectrum version by Richard Jowett who added SAM disk saving and keyboard mapping as the only additions.

The game was actually packaged in the Amstrad CPC packaging, with a label proclaiming it a "SAM Version". This apparently was to overcome the licensing aspect of the game, as well as providing packaging.

459810.overview:
Based on the Amstrad CPC game "Croco Magneto", EGGBum is a fast-paced action puzzle game that is very easy to learn, but difficult to master.

You play as a blob that automatically bounces left and right. All you control is the vertical trajectory of the blob. Collect the jewels, and avoid the skull and crossbones that are littered throughout the mazes.
